# Tides and currents

Tides raise and lower the sea twice a day, and the tidal stream they drive can push a sailing boat faster or slower than the wind can. Plan passages around tide tables and check the depth before [[Anchoring overnight]].

## Rule of twelfths

The tide rises one twelfth of its range in the first hour, two in the second, three in the third and fourth, two in the fifth, one in the sixth.

## Wind against tide

When the wind blows against a strong tidal stream, the sea stands up into steep, short waves. Time headland passages for slack water.
